25/**
26 * @brief Parameters for contact mechanics simulation.
27 *
28 * @note For each field without an actor-pair override, contact between a colliding actor and a
29 * collider uses the collider's contact parameter (not the colliding actor's). The exceptions are:
30 * - For friction and dissipation coefficients (@ref viscousFrictionCoefficient,
31 * @ref coulombFrictionCoefficient, @ref normalViscousDampingCoefficient), the geometric mean of
32 * the colliding and collider's coefficients is used. This disables friction/dissipation if
33 * either of them does.
34 * - For penalty coefficient (@ref penaltyCoefficient), friction velocity threshold
35 * (@ref frictionFalloffVel) and presliding displacement (@ref preslidingDisplacement), the
36 * geometric mean of the colliding and collider's values is used, except if the collider is
37 * static in which case the colliding's values are used.
38 * - Elasto-plastic friction is preferred (@ref preferElastoPlasticFriction) only if both the
39 * colliding and the collider prefer it.
40 *
41 * @see Scene::SetContactPairParamsOverride
42 */
43struct ContactParams {
44 ContactParams() = default;
45
46 /**
47 * @brief Construct ContactParams with all parameters explicitly specified.
48 *
49 * @param[in] penaltyCoefficient See @ref penaltyCoefficient.
50 * @param[in] penaltySmoothingHalfDistance See @ref penaltySmoothingHalfDistance.
51 * @param[in] penaltyThresholdDefault See @ref penaltyThresholdDefault.
52 * @param[in] penaltyThresholdExtraPadding See @ref penaltyThresholdExtraPadding.
53 * @param[in] collidingPenaltyThresholdPadding See @ref collidingPenaltyThresholdPadding.
54 * @param[in] frictionWithColliderNormal See @ref frictionWithColliderNormal.
55 * @param[in] maxAlignmentNormals See @ref maxAlignmentNormals.
56 * @param[in] alignmentSmoothingFraction See @ref alignmentSmoothingFraction.
57 * @param[in] viscousFrictionCoefficient See @ref viscousFrictionCoefficient.
58 * @param[in] coulombFrictionCoefficient See @ref coulombFrictionCoefficient.
59 * @param[in] preferElastoPlasticFriction See @ref preferElastoPlasticFriction.
60 * @param[in] frictionFalloffVel See @ref frictionFalloffVel.
61 * @param[in] preslidingDisplacement See @ref preslidingDisplacement.
62 * @param[in] normalViscousDampingCoefficient See @ref normalViscousDampingCoefficient.
63 * @param[in] distanceErrorBound See @ref distanceErrorBound.
64 * @param[in] objScale See @ref objScale.
65 * @param[in] collidingPenaltyLengthScale See @ref collidingPenaltyLengthScale.
66 *
67 * @note Must take every parameter in order.
68 * @note Used when converting types to/from the C API.
69 */
70 ContactParams(
71 real penaltyCoefficient,
72 real penaltySmoothingHalfDistance,
73 real penaltyThresholdDefault,
74 real penaltyThresholdExtraPadding,
75 real collidingPenaltyThresholdPadding,
76 bool frictionWithColliderNormal,
77 real maxAlignmentNormals,
78 real alignmentSmoothingFraction,
79 real viscousFrictionCoefficient,
80 real coulombFrictionCoefficient,
81 bool preferElastoPlasticFriction,
82 real frictionFalloffVel,
83 real preslidingDisplacement,
84 real normalViscousDampingCoefficient,
85 real distanceErrorBound,
86 real objScale,
87 real collidingPenaltyLengthScale);
88
89 // Parameters for penalty contact.
90
91 /**
92 * @brief Stiffness of the contact penalty force [Pa/m].
93 *
94 * @note Must be finite and strictly positive.
95 * @note Higher penalties create stiffer contacts and reduce penetration.
96 * @note Arbitrarily large penalties may degrade stability.
97 * @note The default penalty is appropriate for actors with default density. For actors with much
98 * higher/lower density than the default density, the penalty coefficient may need to be
99 * increased/decreased accordingly.
100 * @note Without an actor-pair override for this field, the value used in a collision is the
101 * geometric mean of the colliding and collider's coefficients. The exception is if the collider
102 * is static, in which case the colliding's penalty is used.
103 * @note The penalty coefficient is additionally scaled by length-scale corrections when the
104 * colliding or collider integrates contact over a non-2D manifold (e.g., rod, shell). See @ref
105 * collidingPenaltyLengthScale.
106 */
107 real penaltyCoefficient = 1e9_r;
108
109 /**
110 * @brief PolyReLU smoothing half-width [m].
111 *
112 * @details The penalty force transitions from 0 to linear over the decreasing distance range
113 * (penaltyThreshold, penaltyThreshold - 2 * @ref penaltySmoothingHalfDistance).
114 *
115 * @note Must be finite and not negative.
116 * @note Larger smoothing distances improve stability but may increase penetration.
117 * @note Smoothing distance is expected to be small relative to the collider geometry.
118 */
119 real penaltySmoothingHalfDistance = 0.005_r;
120
121 /**
122 * @brief Default contact detection threshold [m].
123 *
124 * @details The penalty force transitions from 0 to linear over the decreasing distance range
125 * (penaltyThreshold, penaltyThreshold - 2 * @ref penaltySmoothingHalfDistance).
126 *
127 * @note Must be finite. Negative values are legal.
128 * @note If the colliding actor has @ref ColliderType::None or @ref ColliderType::PointCloud,
129 * penaltyThreshold = penaltyThresholdDefault + @ref penaltyThresholdExtraPadding. Otherwise,
130 * penaltyThreshold = penaltyThresholdDefault.
131 * @note The colliding actor's @ref collidingPenaltyThresholdPadding, if applicable, is added to
132 * penaltyThreshold.
133 *
134 * @see penaltyThresholdExtraPadding, collidingPenaltyThresholdPadding, GetPenaltyThresholdDist
135 */
136 real penaltyThresholdDefault = 0.001_r;
137
138 /**
139 * @brief [Experimental] Extra padding [m] added to the default contact detection threshold if the
140 * colliding actor has @ref ColliderType::None or @ref ColliderType::PointCloud.
141 *
142 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
143 * your own risk.
144 *
145 * @note Must be finite and not negative.
146 * @note Extra padding is useful to avoid tunneling through thin actors when the other actor has
147 * @ref ColliderType::None or @ref ColliderType::PointCloud.
148 *
149 * @see penaltyThresholdDefault, GetPenaltyThresholdDist
150 */
151 real penaltyThresholdExtraPadding = 0_r;
152
153 /**
154 * @brief [Experimental] Padding [m] added to the collider's contact detection threshold when this
155 * actor is the colliding actor.
156 *
157 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
158 * your own risk.
159 *
160 * @note Must be finite and not negative.
161 * @note Unlike @ref penaltyThresholdExtraPadding, which the collider applies to some colliding
162 * actors, this padding is applied by the colliding actor to any collider, except colliders with
163 * @ref ColliderType::PointCloud and SDF colliders of soft actors, which ignore it.
164 * @note Padding is useful to avoid tunneling of thin or coarsely sampled colliding actors.
165 *
166 * @see penaltyThresholdDefault, penaltyThresholdExtraPadding
167 */
168 real collidingPenaltyThresholdPadding = 0_r;
169
170 // Parameters for friction
171
172 /**
173 * @brief [Experimental] Use collider's normal (normalized SDF gradient) for friction direction if
174 * true, or the colliding's surface normal at the sample point if false.
175 *
176 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
177 * your own risk.
178 *
179 * @note For co-dimensional colliding actors with ambiguous normals, the collider's normal is
180 * always used regardless of frictionWithColliderNormal.
181 */
182 bool frictionWithColliderNormal = true;
183
184 /**
185 * @brief [Experimental] Maximum normal alignment threshold.
186 *
187 * @details Normal alignment is defined as the dot product between colliding and collider normals.
188 * Contact is disabled for sample points whose normal alignment exceeds this threshold, abruptly
189 * or over a band centered at it (see @ref alignmentSmoothingFraction). This prevents sample
190 * points from being trapped inside the collider when penetration is large.
191 *
192 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
193 * your own risk.
194 *
195 * @note Must be in [-1, 1]. -1 allows contact only for perfectly opposing normals. 1 with @ref
196 * alignmentSmoothingFraction = 0 allows all contacts with unit normals. With a smooth band,
197 * contacts at alignment 1 keep half their force.
198 * @note For co-dimensional colliding actors with ambiguous normals, contact is not disabled
199 * regardless of maxAlignmentNormals (normal alignment cannot be computed).
200 *
201 * @see alignmentSmoothingFraction
202 */
203 real maxAlignmentNormals = 0_r;
204
205 /**
206 * @brief [Experimental] Width of the band of normal alignments, centered at @ref
207 * maxAlignmentNormals, over which contact fades out, as a fraction of the range of alignments
208 * [-1, @ref maxAlignmentNormals].
209 *
210 * @details The penalty force of a contact is scaled by a C1 smoothstep of its normal alignment,
211 * from 1 at an alignment of m - w / 2 to 0 at m + w / 2, with m = @ref maxAlignmentNormals and
212 * w = @ref alignmentSmoothingFraction * (m + 1). Contacts at m keep half their force. This
213 * removes the jump of the penalty force when contact is disabled. Contacts beyond the band are
214 * disabled, and friction fading (@ref ExperimentalEvalParams::fadeFriction) ends at its top.
215 *
216 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
217 * your own risk.
218 *
219 * @note Must be in [0, 1]. 0 disables contact abruptly at @ref maxAlignmentNormals.
220 * @note With the default 0.1 and the default @ref maxAlignmentNormals = 0, contact between unit
221 * normals fades out between angles of 92.9 and 87.1 degrees (a 5.7-degree band).
222 * @note Applies only with implicit normals (@ref ExperimentalEvalParams::explicitNormals =
223 * false). With explicit normals, contact is disabled abruptly at @ref maxAlignmentNormals.
224 * @note For co-dimensional colliding actors with ambiguous normals, the scale is 1 (normal
225 * alignment cannot be computed).
226 *
227 * @see maxAlignmentNormals
228 */
229 real alignmentSmoothingFraction = 0.1_r;
230
231 /**
232 * @brief Viscous friction coefficient [s/m].
233 *
234 * @note Friction force is proportional to contact force and tangential velocity.
235 * @note Must be finite and not negative.
236 * @note Both viscousFrictionCoefficient and @ref coulombFrictionCoefficient can be >0.
237 * @note Without an actor-pair override for this field, the value used in a collision is the
238 * geometric mean of the colliding and collider's coefficients. This disables viscous friction if
239 * either of them does.
240 */
241 real viscousFrictionCoefficient = 0_r;
242
243 /**
244 * @brief Coulomb friction coefficient (dimensionless).
245 *
246 * @note Must be finite and not negative.
247 * @note Both @ref viscousFrictionCoefficient and coulombFrictionCoefficient can be >0.
248 * @note Without an actor-pair override for this field, the value used in a collision is the
249 * geometric mean of the colliding and collider's coefficients. This disables Coulomb friction if
250 * either of them does.
251 */
252 real coulombFrictionCoefficient = 0.5_r;
253
254 /**
255 * @brief [Experimental] Prefer elasto-plastic Coulomb friction to velocity-regularized Coulomb
256 * friction.
257 *
258 * @details Elasto-plastic friction measures the tangential displacement of each contact from its
259 * anchor, a point of the collider, so a contact holds a tangential load below the Coulomb limit
260 * without slip (see @ref preslidingDisplacement). Velocity-regularized friction acts only through
261 * slip, so held objects creep (see @ref frictionFalloffVel).
262 *
263 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
264 * your own risk.
265 *
266 * @note Contacts that prefer elasto-plastic friction use it where it is supported: with rigid
267 * colliders, static or dynamic, including articulated links, and with an integration method whose
268 * step ends at its last stage (@ref IntegrationMethod::BackwardEuler,
269 * @ref IntegrationMethod::BDF2, @ref IntegrationMethod::BDF3, @ref IntegrationMethod::DIRK22 or
270 * @ref IntegrationMethod::DIRK33). The other contacts use velocity-regularized friction.
271 * @note Friction preload is part of the actor history (see @ref Actor). A static actor given a
272 * velocity every step, like a conveyor belt, never builds preload, so contacts on it creep, as
273 * with velocity-regularized friction whose falloff velocity is @ref preslidingDisplacement over
274 * the stage step (the time step with @ref IntegrationMethod::BackwardEuler).
275 * @note Without an actor-pair override for this field, a collision prefers elasto-plastic
276 * friction only if both the colliding and the collider do, even if the collider is static.
277 */
278 bool preferElastoPlasticFriction = true;
279
280 /**
281 * @brief [Experimental] Velocity threshold for Coulomb friction smoothing [m/s].
282 *
283 * @details The Coulomb friction force smoothly transitions from 0 to full strength as tangential
284 * velocity increases from 0 to frictionFalloffVel.
285 *
286 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
287 * your own risk.
288 *
289 * @note Must be finite and not negative. Zero gives unsmoothed Coulomb friction.
290 * @note Used only by contacts with velocity-regularized friction (see
291 * @ref preferElastoPlasticFriction).
292 * @note Smaller velocity thresholds improve physical accuracy but may degrade stability.
293 * @note Without an actor-pair override for this field, the value used in a collision is the
294 * geometric mean of the colliding and collider's thresholds. The exception is if the collider is
295 * static, in which case the colliding's threshold is used.
296 */
297 real frictionFalloffVel = 0.01_r;
298
299 /**
300 * @brief Presliding displacement of elasto-plastic Coulomb friction [m].
301 *
302 * @details With elasto-plastic friction (see @ref preferElastoPlasticFriction), the Coulomb
303 * friction force smoothly transitions from 0 to full strength as the tangential displacement of a
304 * contact from its anchor increases from 0 to preslidingDisplacement, and beyond it the anchor
305 * follows the contact. A held contact springs back by up to preslidingDisplacement once the load
306 * is removed.
307 *
308 * @note Smaller values reduce presliding motion and spring-back, but stiffen the tangential
309 * response.
310 * @note Within the presliding displacement, the friction force is elastic: it stores energy and
311 * adds no damping. Tangential damping comes only from @ref viscousFrictionCoefficient, zero by
312 * default, and from the time integration (@ref normalViscousDampingCoefficient acts along the
313 * normal).
314 * @note Must be finite and strictly positive.
315 * @note Without an actor-pair override for this field, the value used in a collision is the
316 * geometric mean of the colliding and collider's displacements. The exception is if the collider
317 * is static, in which case the colliding's displacement is used.
318 */
319 real preslidingDisplacement = 1e-4_r;
320
321 /**
322 * @brief Normal viscous damping coefficient [s/m].
323 *
324 * @details Damping force in the normal direction, proportional to the elastic normal contact
325 * force and the normal velocity. Analogous to @ref viscousFrictionCoefficient but acting in the
326 * normal direction instead of tangentially.
327 *
328 * @warning The calibration diverges as CoR approaches zero, which may cause numerical problems
329 * when approaching fully-inelastic collisions.
330 *
331 * @note Must be finite and not negative.
332 * @note Without an actor-pair override for this field, the value used in a collision is the
333 * geometric mean of the colliding and collider's coefficients. This disables normal damping if
334 * either of them does.
335 * @note The resulting coefficient of restitution (CoR) is velocity-dependent. For a
336 * characteristic impact velocity,
337 * @c experimental::CalibrateNormalViscousDampingCoefficient computes the coefficient that
338 * approximates a target CoR, while @c experimental::EffectiveCoefficientOfRestitution recovers
339 * the CoR produced by a coefficient.
340 * @note Because the damping force depends on the normal velocity at each contact point, it also
341 * introduces rolling resistance: a body rolling on a surface dissipates energy through the
342 * differing normal velocities across its contacting region.
343 */
344 real normalViscousDampingCoefficient = 0_r;
345
346 // Experimental parameters
347
348 /**
349 * @brief [Experimental] Padding [m] added to the collider's bounding volume for collision
350 * culling.
351 *
352 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
353 * your own risk.
354 *
355 * @note Must be finite.
356 * @note Useful, for example, with approximate SDFs (e.g., deep flow map) to compensate for
357 * potentially overestimating the true distance.
358 */
359 real distanceErrorBound = 0_r;
360
361 /**
362 * @brief [Experimental] Object scale relative to default size (dimensionless). Used by deep flow
363 * only.
364 *
365 * @warning Deep flow is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use
366 * at your own risk.
367 *
368 * @note Must be finite and strictly positive.
369 */
370 real objScale = 1_r;
371
372 /**
373 * @brief [Experimental] Length scale [m] used to correct the penalty coefficient when the
374 * colliding body integrates contact traction over a lower-than-two-dimensional manifold, such as
375 * a rod or point mass. E.g., the penalty is scaled by this value if the colliding body lumps
376 * contact tractions on a line, or this value squared if lumping contact forces on a point.
377 *
378 * @warning Contact with lower-dimensional bodies is an experimental feature. It may be changed or
379 * removed in the future. Use at your own risk.
380 *
381 * @note Must be finite and strictly positive.
382 * @note This value is not used in the most common case, where contact traction is integrated over
383 * a two-dimensional surface.
384 * @note The colliding body's value is always used in a contact pair, because the colliding body
385 * determines the dimension of the contact traction integral.
386 */
387 real collidingPenaltyLengthScale = 1_r;
388
389 /**
390 * @brief Get the total contact detection threshold.
391 *
392 * @param addPadding If true, includes @ref penaltyThresholdExtraPadding.
393 *
394 * @return Total contact detection threshold [m].
395 */
396 real GetPenaltyThresholdDist(bool addPadding) const;

425/**
426 * @brief Collision detection geometry for an @ref Actor.
427 *
428 * @note This setting controls how OTHER actors detect contact with this actor. It does not affect
429 * how this actor detects contact with other actors.
430 */
431enum class ColliderType {
432 /**
433 * @brief No collision representation. Other actors cannot detect contact with this actor.
434 *
435 * @note It does NOT prevent this actor from detecting contact with other actors.
436 */
437 None,
438
439 /**
440 * @brief Automatic collider type selection based on the actor's shape.
441 *
442 * @note Mochi will select the most appropriate collider type based on the actor's shape and type:
443 * - Implicit sphere shapes: @ref ColliderType::Sphere
444 * - Implicit plane shapes: @ref ColliderType::Plane
445 * - Mesh shapes on volumetric actors (e.g., rigid, soft): @ref ColliderType::Sdf
446 * - Shell and rod actors: @ref ColliderType::PointCloud
447 *
448 * @note If Auto is set on an actor, a valid collider type will be assigned even if the shape's
449 * default collider type is @ref ColliderType::None. If you want @ref ColliderType::None, set
450 * @ref ColliderType::None explicitly as your collider type.
451 *
452 * @note After initialization, @ref Actor::GetColliderType will return the selected type, not
453 * @ref ColliderType::Auto.
454 */
455 Auto,
456
457 /**
458 * @brief Represent the actor by an approximating sphere derived from its bounding volume.
459 *
460 * @note For shapes with a sphere bounding volume, that sphere is used. For shapes with an
461 * OBB/AABB bounding volume, the inscribed sphere is used. Otherwise, a true bounding sphere is
462 * computed.
463 * @note Fast but only accurate for spherical geometries.
464 * @note Only supported for rigid actors and articulated links.
465 */
466 Sphere,
467
468 /**
469 * @brief Represent the actor by its axis-aligned bounding box (AABB), in the actor's local frame.
470 *
471 * @note Fast but only accurate for box geometries.
472 * @note Only supported for rigid actors and articulated links.
473 */
474 Box,
475
476 /**
477 * @brief [Experimental] Represent the actor by its surface mesh.
478 *
479 * @warning Mesh collision performs triangle-mesh distance queries during simulation and can be
480 * prohibitively slow. For mesh-backed actors, prefer @ref ColliderType::Auto or
481 * @ref ColliderType::Sdf unless measurements justify using Mesh.
482 * @warning This is an experimental feature. It may be changed or removed in the future. Use at
483 * your own risk.
484 *
485 * @note Only supported for rigid actors and articulated links.
486 */
487 Mesh,
488
489 /**
490 * @brief Represent the actor as an infinite plane.
491 *
492 * @note Only supported for static rigid actors whose shape is an implicit plane.
493 */
494 Plane,
495
496 /**
497 * @brief Grid-based Signed Distance Field (SDF) collision representation.
498 *
499 * @note Uses a 3D grid storing the distance to the closest point in the actor's surface.
500 * @note Accurate for closed non-intersecting geometries provided the grid resolution is
501 * sufficient.
502 * @note If the grid is not baked in the actor's Shape, it is computed at initialization
503 * (expensive), and actor creation fails if it cannot be computed.
504 * @note Also supported for soft actors via SDF mapping.
505 *
506 * @see GridSdfParams
507 */
508 Sdf,
509
510 /**
511 * @brief Point-cloud collision representation.
512 *
513 * @details Contacts are detected by proximity queries between collider-side sample points and
514 * colliding-side sample points. Only other point-cloud colliders can collide with this type.
515 */
516 PointCloud,
517
518 /** @brief Number of collider type enum values. */
519 Count
520};
521} // namespace superdex
